note: The floor-space segment's narration (twin/video/floorspace_cut.py): Kokoro v1.0, voice af_heart, as the campaign video. Each line names the phase it is spoken in (at: seconds into that phase) and what on screen it says (shows). Numbers are as layouts.json has them. The plans phase leads to the capacity-matched comparison (f11, f12: the Shuttles' 45 trays laid out flat against the vertical lab), which is the segment's result; today's 43 instruments (f8) and Emerald Cloud Lab (f10) are context before it. cues: seconds into a line's recording at which a word is said (`python -m twin.video.floorspace_voice words f8 f11 f12`), where floorspace_cut brings in what the word names.

lines.text: Forty-three instruments, laid out three ways. These are design layouts, not built labs.
lines.shows: title: 43 instruments, three layouts; 'design layouts, not built labs'

lines.text: First, a conventional materials lab, grouped by workflow: rooms for powder, the metal printers, the machine shop, the furnace and the SEM, and open benches for the rest.
Benches are thirty inches deep and aisles five feet wide, with service space behind every floor machine. Measured to its walls, it comes to 4,280 square feet.
lines.shows: the rules box; the area panel: 4,280 sq ft

lines.text: Next, the same floor plan, automated. Mobile robots drive the routes people walked, with fixed arms, docking targets and sample racks at the stations.
The floor area stays the same. And a robot docked in a five-foot aisle leaves too little room for another to pass.
lines.shows: area panel unchanged; the aisle note

lines.text: The vertical lab. Two Kardex Shuttles come in, and every benchtop instrument moves onto a tray.
lines.shows: Shuttles label; '31 benchtop instruments onto trays'

lines.text: The floor machines rearrange along one robot aisle, and the floor area falls to 3,029 square feet.
Side by side. For today's 43 instruments, a flat lab laid out so robots can dock and pass needs 4,128 square feet, about what the conventional lab does.
lines.shows: row 1, labelled as context: the four plans for today's 43 instruments at one scale; the layout for robots picked out, 4,128 sq ft, beside the conventional lab's 4,280

lines.text: For scale, Emerald Cloud Lab in South San Francisco held more than a hundred items of equipment in about 15,000 square feet.
But today's equipment uses only 18 of the Shuttles' 45 trays. Laid out flat, as bench positions robots can serve, all 45 need 6,192 square feet.
lines.shows: row 2, the result: 'Same capacity: the Shuttles' 45 trays as bench positions', '18 trays in use today, 27 more'; the 45 positions laid out flat, 6,192 sq ft

lines.text: The vertical lab holds them in 3,029: 51 percent less floor, at 14.9 tray positions per thousand square feet, against 7.3.
lines.shows: row 2: the vertical lab, 3,029 sq ft, the badge 'minus 51 %', '14.9 against 7.3 tray positions per 1,000 sq ft'; the title becomes the result

lines.text: In the vertical lab, most of the floor goes to the floor machines, their clearances and the robot aisle, the same as in the flat layouts for robots. And the Shuttles stand 9.15 meters tall, so it needs a high bay.
lines.shows: the bars: the floor machines' block, the same in the vertical lab and both layouts for robots, and the benchtop part; 'Shuttles 9.15 m tall: a high bay'
